newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Cash-strapped Geneva daily to merge with rival.
newsitem.headline: Cash-strapped Geneva daily to merge with rival.

text.p: Geneva's oldest newspaper, the French-language Journal de Geneve, announced on Wednesday that it will merge with rival daily Swiss newspaper Le Nouveau Quotidien to overcome its financial difficulties.

Le Journal de Geneve, battling for survival, said in a front-page letter to its readers that tough competition in the media business had forced the merger to create a new newspaper called the new Nouveau Journal.

The two loss-making dailies first entered merger talks last year. But the talks collapsed mainly because of the different sizes of the two publishers, SA du Journal de Geneve and the Edipresse Group which controls the Lausanne-based Nouveau Quotidien.
The merger is pending approval by the Federal competition authorities, Swiss news agency ATS reported.

Rival Geneva daily, Tribune de Geneve, lamented the Journal de Geneve's disappearance in a front-page editorial. "One more page in the history of Geneva has been turned. We will miss our Journal," it said.
The Journal de Geneve, with a daily circulation of around 32,000 copies, suffered losses of nearly two million Swiss francs ($1.4 million) in 1996 but had aimed to break even in 1997.
Sources at the paper said redundancies were not ruled out as a result of the merger.
The two newspapers have distinctive identities. Le Journal de Geneve, founded in 1826, is a quality daily with a long tradition of serious reporting.

The Nouveau Quotidien, founded five years ago with Jacques Pilet as editor, is also a quality daily but has aimed at younger readers and a greater emphasis on feature articles. Its publisher Edipresse Group dominates French-speaking Switzerland. ($ = 1.439 Swiss Francs)
